core_claim: In spring 2020 democracies cut population mobility further than autocracies — even at the same level of legal stringency — overturning the early-pandemic narrative that authoritarian regimes were structurally better at containing epidemics.

edt_01.label: Hook: the gap nobody expected
edt_01.title: When the order to stay home meets free citizens
edt_01.editorial_notes: Lead with the 13.7pp retail & rec. gap. Do not round.

edt_02.label: Three months of the same picture
edt_02.title: Three months. Five categories. The same gap.
edt_02.editorial_notes: Show the full month x category x regime grid as the central chart.

edt_03.label: Stringency vs compliance
edt_03.title: Stricter laws are not the answer
edt_03.editorial_notes: Stringency 79.3 vs 80.6 must be shown as visually near-equal; mobility gap is the surprise.

edt_04.label: The country dots
edt_04.title: Every country, two numbers
edt_04.editorial_notes: Highlight Japan and Sweden as the right kind of exceptions — voluntary distancing without strict orders.

edt_05.label: Long before COVID
edt_05.title: Sixty years of epidemics tell the same story
edt_05.editorial_notes: Note that under-reporting biases the comparison toward autocracies looking better than they are; finding is conservative.

edt_06.label: What this means
edt_06.title: Compliance, not coercion
edt_06.editorial_notes: Land on 'will anyone listen?' — avoid triumphalism.
